name: l1_tecs
comment: Classical autopilot for FixedwingWaypointsEnv: L1 lateral guidance (Park-Deyst-Howe 2004) -> bank command; TECS (Lambregts 1983, simplified total-energy form) -> throttle (P+I on specific-energy error) and pitch command (P on energy-balance error); inner roll/pitch loops are PD on angle with body-rate damping on the env's surface interface. Angles in this file use the env's euler convention (x fwd, y left, z up): positive roll = right bank, positive pitch = NOSE DOWN. Terminal-convergence features (tuned on train seed 7 diagnostics, 2026-10-21): distance-scheduled L1 (a constant L1 sustains a stable limit-cycle orbit at r ~= L1/(2 sin eta) outside the 10 m capture sphere), aerodynamic bank limit bank_max = acos((v_stall/V)^2) from n_max = (V/v_stall)^2 (the previous linear ramp made the minimum turn radius WORSE as airspeed dropped), and distance-based speed bleed so the endgame pursuit radius stays below the approach distance. Overspeed climb trade (k_geo_up): when the scheduled airspeed is below the current one and altitude is wanted, pitch up beyond trim to convert kinetic energy into climb -- the TECS balance term alone is neutralised by the coexisting speed deficit (h_err and dv cancel in the total-energy error), leaving the airframe overspeed on spiral arcs that exceed the OOB sphere; the speed-keep term is clamped to the underspeed side so it can no longer push the nose down on overspeed. (Throttle-side overspeed governors were tried and rejected: an output cap below trim destroys the integrator's trim estimate and mushes the airframe; an energy-error clamp forbids climb power at the scheduled airspeed. The climb-out overspeed is left to the pitch trade.) Anti-windup bleed requires the energy error to be a genuine surplus (dE < 0). Climb-phase containment (h_loiter_gate, pn_loiter) blends the lateral aim toward the origin when the target is far above and the aircraft far out; DISABLED in the shipped configuration (h_loiter_gate = 1e4) because it measured net-negative on the train split. pitch_up_max_deg raised 10 -> 16 in the 2026-10-22 tuning sweep: the 10 deg nose-up clamp was throttling the power-limited climb (18 N thrust < 23 N weight), which was the DOMINANT out-of-bounds mode (forensics: OOB episodes died with the active waypoint 50-90 m above and 66-101 m away, airspeed pinned at the energy-optimal 23 m/s where the turn radius is 31-64 m -- unrecoverable inside the 100 m sphere). At 16 deg the high-target episodes can actually climb home: OOB 23.9% -> 1.8%, crash rate stays 0.0 (no accelerated-stall penalty; the (V-v_min)/(v_full-v_min) speed schedule keeps the clamp closed at low airspeed). 18 deg measured identical (94.9% vs 94.7%); 16 kept for stall margin. Other 2026-10-22 levers measured net-negative and were rejected: loiter containment re-enabled (73.8%), range-scheduled speed bleed k_pn_bleed (73.3-74.2%), k_geo_up 0.8/1.0 (73.5/71.4%). Residual failure mode (1.8%): very high targets still time out climbing. Tuned only on training/development initial conditions (train seed 7, dev seeds 1000-1003).
